entries.title: Document for humans and machines
entries.summary: The user requires persistent repository memory readable by any AI provider, with human-readable and machine-readable documentation kept current together.
details: Maintain MEMORY.md and MEMORY.json together as knowledge changes; a chat transcript or provider-private memory is insufficient.
For behavior or interface changes, also maintain the relevant human guides and existing machine contracts.

entries.title: Mac Control architecture and documentation
entries.summary: Mac Control is a self-hosted macOS dashboard for controls, cooling, USB storage, and system activity.
details: The server uses the Python standard library; native helpers use Objective-C and macOS frameworks; the frontend uses plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
README.md describes user-facing behavior; docs/REFERENCE.md covers implementation and maintenance; docs/machines/mbp15.md is the machine runbook.
docs/API.md covers the full Mac Control HTTP API; packages/contracts/README.md identifies local API contracts and the separate Notifier exports.
DevBox Notifier is a separate optional service. Its integration guide is docs/integrations/mac-control.md; machine contracts live in packages/contracts/.

entries.title: Mac Control HTTP interface
entries.summary: Mac Control's full HTTP API and the first integration use case are documented in docs/API.md, packages/contracts/mac-control.openapi.json and packages/contracts/mac-control-api.json.
details: The current implementation has 21 GET/POST operations under /api/. The API documentation revision is 1.1.1; the runtime has no negotiated API version or live OpenAPI route. Hardware response schemas remain extensible.

Requests require private/loopback/link-local source and known Host/port checks; cross-site fetches are rejected. POST requires an exact http://Host Origin and a JSON object from 1 through 4096 bytes, even for login and logout.

Private routes use the mac_control cookie, with fixed 24-hour normal or 30-day remembered expiry. Session inspection, sign-in, first setup and stats/leave do not require a valid session; setup requires loopback and leave can remove only the supplied cookie/viewer lease. There is no Mac Control bearer-token API.

Maintain the guide, local OpenAPI, API/use-case manifest and both memory files together as behavior changes. packages/contracts/openapi.json is the separate Notifier API, not the full Mac Control API.

entries.title: First API integration: Notifier copy progress
entries.summary: The user identified DevBox Notifier copy progress as the first API integration use case; this does not establish a historical deployment date.
details: The browser polls GET /api/file-activity with its Mac Control session. After authorization, the server pulls GET /v1/snapshot over fixed loopback using a private administrator bearer from configured state_dir/admin-token. Notifier does not POST activity into Mac Control; notifications/streaming are separate.

The bridge uses a two-second timeout, a 2 MiB response cap and no environment proxies. Caught upstream/configuration failures return HTTP 200 available=false with empty activity lists; this is not evidence that no copy is running.

Each visible authenticated client waits two seconds after request completion before polling again. The local UI shows up to eight qualifying active copies, overall progress and a current filename summary; unavailable/error responses hide the section. English operation/measured-detail filters can omit localized Finder observations. Window disappearance does not prove completion.

The separate Notifier repository owns the five exported version 1.1.0 activity contracts (2026-11-01). Local API/use-case documents describe this checkout; reading them is not a live check of the separate Notifier service.

entries.title: This checkout is the live installation
entries.summary: The execution machine is mbp15, and this checkout is its live Mac Control installation according to the machine runbook.
details: The checkout is /Users/paolo/personal/mac-control. The user launch agent is ~/Library/LaunchAgents/local.maccontrol.server.plist, label local.maccontrol.server; the dashboard uses port 8765.
Before managing the service, run python3 service.py status to verify the active location. Do not start a second server on port 8765 or move/remove the checkout while the launch agent points here.

Frontend changes are live. Python changes require a dashboard restart; native changes use the installer. Dashboard management does not require restarting privileged fan or input helpers. An input-helper restart resets both built-in inputs to On.
The old ~/Library/Application Support/Mac Control/.runtime compatibility symlink must remain for existing permission and notifier paths.

entries.title: Preserve private runtime and backups
entries.summary: Runtime state and migration backups are private, untracked local data that must be preserved.
details: .runtime/ contains credentials, sessions, settings, compiled helpers, and logs. .local-backups/ contains private migration backups.
Never commit, upload, copy into memory, or replace these directories with fixtures or another installation's state.
Preserve saved state and the existing compatibility symlink during updates.

entries.title: Match checks to the change
entries.summary: Use the repository's documented checks when relevant; recording a command here does not mean it has been run.
details: The Python test suite is python3 -m unittest discover.
Native build preflight is ./install.command --check.
Check the active installation with python3 service.py status before service management. Documentation-only work needs no service restart.

entries.title: Read-only host battery and Tailscale indicators
entries.summary: The dashboard has a compact host battery gauge and Tailscale status strip above System activity.
details: GET /api/host-status requires a session and returns only battery and Tailscale summaries from read-only local commands; no peer or account data.

Reads use two-second command timeouts and a shared ten-second demand-driven cache. The visible authenticated browser polls ten seconds after completion; hidden, signed-out and unloaded pages pause polling.

Tailscale connected requires BackendState=Running and Self.Online=true. Missing CLI, login/approval needs, disconnected and unavailable states are explicit; unknown battery readings do not become zero.

entries.title: Stable mobile tabs and chart inspection
entries.summary: Mobile section buttons preserve their screen position, and charts support sample inspection.
details: Mobile uses sticky tabs, content-sized panes and a viewport-sized minimum workspace; tab focus and section switching preserve scroll position. USB cards retain DOM identity across polls.

Overview, expanded and daily energy charts support mouse hover, tap and keyboard inspection with Manila time and units. Values come from recorded samples; missing samples are not interpolated. Expand icons have separate 44px targets.

entries.title: Separate password unlock from normal mounting
entries.summary: Encrypted-drive mounting requests passwords only for locked targets and preserves mount errors for unlocked targets.
details: Unlock actions request mounted=true even for partially mounted drives. Password submissions explicitly request Mount; older in-flight polls cannot overwrite an action result.

The Python manager invokes native unlock only when fresh metadata reports a locked target. Native already-unlocked targets return the normal mount result directly; requiresPassword is reserved for targets still locked.

Unlock diagnostics use fixed authentication, privacy (TCC), permission or general messages in the API, without raw command output. On failure the helper writes diskutil's stderr (never the password) to its stderr, which drives.py logs to .runtime/server.log. Passwords remain stdin-only and are never saved.

diskutil error -69464 ('restricted by sandbox') is a TCC Removable Volumes denial; the background service cannot show the consent prompt, so Terminal unlocks succeed while the dashboard fails. TCC attributes requests to the launch agent's first executable, so the agent runs the Command Line Tools Python.app binary directly (identifier com.apple.python3), not caffeinate or the /usr/bin/python3 shim, and server.py starts `caffeinate -is -w <pid>` when MAC_CONTROL_STAY_AWAKE=1. On mbp15 that Python.app has Full Disk Access (granted 2026-11-03). Disk-image volumes are not subject to this check, so test images do not reproduce it.
